chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Ajlan al-Marwazi al-Muqri narrated that Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Jurjani narrated that Abu Bakr Abd al-Samad ibn Yahya al-Wasiti narrated that al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Madani from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated:

He said: Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, created the light of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) before He created the heavens and the earth, the Throne, the Footstool, the Tablet, the Pen, Paradise and Hellfire, and before He created Adam, Noah, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, David, and Solomon, and all whom God, the Mighty and Majestic, mentions in His saying, 'And We gave him Isaac and Jacob... to His saying: And We guided them to a straight path.' And before He created all the Prophets by four hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand years.

And God, the Mighty and Majestic, created with him twelve veils: the veil of Power, the veil of Grandeur, the veil of Grace, the veil of Mercy, the veil of Bliss, the veil of Munificence, the veil of Station, the veil of Guidance, the veil of Prophethood, the veil of Eminence, the veil of Awe, and the veil of Intercession.

Then the light of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was confined in the veil of Power for twelve thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to my Lord, the Most High.' And in the veil of Grandeur for eleven thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to the Knower of the Secret.' And in the veil of Grace for ten thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to Him who is Everlasting, never playful.' And in the veil of Mercy for nine thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to the Elevated, the Most High.' And in the veil of Bliss for eight thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to Him who is Everlasting, never heedless.' And in the veil of Munificence for seven thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to Him who is Rich, never needy.' And in the veil of Station for six thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to my Lord, the Most High, the Most Generous.' And in the veil of Guidance for five thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to the Lord of the Great Throne.' And in the veil of Prophethood for four thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to the Lord of Honor, above what they describe.' And in the veil of Eminence for three thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to the Possessor of Sovereignty and Dominion.' And in the veil of Awe for two thousand years, and it said: 'Glory to God and praise be to Him.' And in the veil of Intercession for one thousand year, and it said: 'Glory to my Lord, the Great, and praise be to Him.'

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, made His name appear on the Tablet, and it remained illuminated on the Tablet for four thousand years. Then He made it appear on the Throne, and it remained fixed on the leg of the Throne for seven thousand years until God, the Mighty and Majestic, placed it in the loins of Adam. Then He transferred it from the loins of Adam to the loins of Noah. Then He caused it to emerge from one loin to another until He brought it out from the loins of Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib.

Then He honored him with six nobilities: He clothed him in the shirt of Contentment, wrapped him in the cloak of Awe, crowned him with the crown of Guidance, dressed him in the trousers of Knowledge, made his sash the sash of Love with which he tied his trousers, made his shoes Fear, and handed him the cane of Station.
Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said to him: 'O Muhammad, go to the people and tell them: Say, there is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God.'

And the origin of that shirt was in six things: its body was of ruby, its sleeves were of pearl, its gussets were of yellow crystal, its underarms were of chrysolite, its collar was of red coral, and its chest was of the Light of the Lord, may His Majesty be Exalted.

So God accepted the repentance of Adam (peace be upon him) because of that shirt, and returned Solomon's ring by it, and returned Joseph to Jacob by it, and saved Jonah from the belly of the whale by it, and thus all the other Prophets (peace be upon them) He saved from trials by it, and that shirt was none other than the shirt of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

The compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: The souls of all the Imams (peace be upon them) and the believers were created with the soul of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أَرْوَاحُ الْأَئِمَّةِ: Souls of the Imams, indicating their pre-existence with Muhammad's soul
key_terms.حِجَاب: Veil, representing a layer of divine manifestation or concealment
key_terms.صَلْب: Loins, referring to the lineage of prophetic transmission
key_terms.قَمِيصُ الرِّضَا: Shirt of Contentment, a spiritual garment of Muhammad
key_terms.نُورُ مُحَمَّدٍ: The Light of Muhammad, a metaphysical entity created before all else

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and nature of the light of Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Ala al-Nur* (Primordial Light), positing Muhammad’s light as the first creation from which all other entities, including the twelve veils of divine attributes, emanated. It details the transmission of this light through the loins of the prophets, culminating in the spiritual attire of Muhammad, which served as the instrument for the salvation of previous prophets. This narrative underscores the metaphysical precedence of the Prophet and the continuity of the Imamate as an extension of this primordial light.
